paper.title_en: Possible Sources of Iron Nuclei in Ultra-High-Energy Cosmic Rays
paper.abstract_en: The origin of a cosmic-ray particle with an ultra-high energy of $2.44\times 10^{20}$ eV recorded by the Telescope Array is discussed by assuming that it is a heavy nucleus, namely an iron or silicon nucleus. Iron is chosen as the heaviest element in cosmic rays, while silicon is chosen to find out how much the theoretical results obtained vary with the mass of the heavy nucleus. The constraints on the distances to the possible extragalactic sources of a heavy particle with such an energy are analyzed by assuming an extragalactic origin of this particle and using a routine calculation of the origin of cosmic rays in intergalactic space. These sources are discussed.
